subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar accept an opt-in feature that launches user-configured local executables in response to background quota and provider events?
rationale: The implementation contains meaningful mitigations, but whether CodexBar should own this persistent background code-execution surface is a product and security-boundary choice that automated review cannot make.

options.title: Accept hooks after argv repair
options.body: Approve the direct-exec boundary, require lossless argument editing and regression proof, then review the exact repaired head for merge.

options.title: Narrow the initial surface
options.body: Start with shared config and CLI management while deferring the graphical editor or automatic background execution.

options.title: Decline local execution
options.body: Keep CodexBar observability-only and leave event automation to an external polling or integration process.

recommendation.title: Accept hooks after argv repair
recommendation.body: Approve the direct-exec boundary, require lossless argument editing and regression proof, then review the exact repaired head for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, this person is the clearest available authority for a new persistent configuration and local process-execution contract.
